     2→

    17→
    18→<details>
    19→<summary>Milestone 1: Staging MVP (Phases 1-10) -- SHIPPED 2026-02-11</summary>
    20→
    21→- [x] **Phase 1: Foundation** - Project scaffolding, CI/CD, development environment

    26→- [x] **Phase 4.2: Local IPFS Testing Infrastructure** - Add local IPFS node to Docker for offline testing (INSERTED)
    27→- [x] **Phase 5: Folder System** - IPNS metadata, folder hierarchy, and operations
    28→- [x] **Phase 6: File Browser UI** - Web interface for file management
    29→- [x] **Phase 6.1: Webapp Automation Testing** - E2E UI testing with automation framework (INSERTED)
    30→- [x] **Phase 6.2: Restyle App with Pencil Design** - Complete UI redesign using Pencil design tool (INSERTED)
    31→- [x] **Phase 6.3: UI Structure Refactor** - Page layouts, component hierarchy, and structural redesign using Pencil (INSERTED)
    32→- [x] **Phase 7: Multi-Device Sync** - IPNS polling and sync state management
    33→- [x] **Phase 7.1: Atomic File Upload** - Refactor multi-request upload into single atomic backend call with batch IPNS publishing (INSERTED)
    34→- [x] **Phase 8: TEE Integration** - Auto-republishing via Phala Cloud
    35→- [x] **Phase 9: Desktop Client** - Tauri app with FUSE mount for macOS
    36→- [x] **Phase 9.1: Environment Changes, DevOps & Staging Deployment** - CI/CD, environment config, staging deploy (INSERTED)

    43→</details>
    44→
    45→### Milestone 2: Production v1.0 (In Progress)
    46→
    47→**Milestone Goal:** Elevate the staging MVP into a production-ready encrypted storage platform with sharing, search, MFA, file versioning, cross-platform desktop, and TEE failover.
    48→
    49→- [ ] **Phase 11: Cross-Platform Desktop** - Linux and Windows desktop apps (Tauri, platform-specific FUSE/virtual drive) -- can run in parallel
    50→- [x] **Phase 11.1: macOS Desktop Catch-Up** - Close all desktop gaps from Phases 12-12.6 before cross-platform expansion (INSERTED)
    51→- [x] **Phase 12: Core Kit Identity Provider Foundation** - Replace PnP Modal SDK with MPC Core Kit, CipherBox as identity provider
    52→- [x] **Phase 12.1: AES-CTR Streaming Encryption** - AES-256-CTR for media files with byte-range decryption and in-browser playback (INSERTED)
    53→- [x] **Phase 12.2: Encrypted Device Registry** - Encrypted device metadata on IPFS for cross-device infrastructure (INSERTED)
    54→- [x] **Phase 12.3: SIWE + Unified Identity** - Wallet login via SIWE, multi-auth linking, ADR-001 cleanup (INSERTED)
    55→- [x] **Phase 12.3.1: Pre-Wipe Identity Cleanup** - Deterministic IPNS derivation, hashed identifiers, remove auto-linking (INSERTED)
    56→- [x] **Phase 12.4: MFA + Cross-Device Approval** - MFA enrollment, recovery phrase, factor management, device approval flow (INSERTED)
    57→- [x] **Phase 12.5: MFA Polishing, UAT & E2E Testing** - Polish auth flows, wallet E2E with mock provider, fix UAT bugs (INSERTED)
    58→- [x] **Phase 12.6: Per-File IPNS Metadata Split** - Split file metadata into per-file IPNS records, decouple content updates from folder publishes (INSERTED)
    59→- [x] **Phase 11.2: Remove v1 Folder Metadata** - Eliminate v1/v2 dual-schema, make v2 FilePointer canonical, per-file IPNS in desktop FUSE (INSERTED)
    60→- [x] **Phase 13: File Versioning** - Automatic version retention with history view and restore
    61→- [x] **Phase 14: User-to-User Sharing** - Read-only folder and file sharing with ECIES key re-wrapping
    62→- [ ] **Phase 15: Link Sharing** - Shareable file links for non-users with URL-fragment decryption keys
    63→- [ ] **Phase 15.1: Client-Side Search** - Encrypted search index in IndexedDB with incremental updates (INSERTED)
    64→- [ ] **Phase 16: Advanced Sync** - Conflict detection, offline queue, and idempotent replay
    65→- [ ] **Phase 17: AWS Nitro TEE** - Nitro enclave as fallback TEE provider for IPNS republishing
    66→
    67→### Milestone 3: Encrypted Productivity Suite (Planned)
    68→
    69→**Milestone Goal:** Transform CipherBox into an encrypted productivity platform with billing, team accounts, document editors, and document signing.
    70→
    71→- [ ] **Phase 18: Billing Infrastructure** - Stripe subscriptions, NOWPayments crypto billing, tier enforcement
    72→- [ ] **Phase 19: Team Accounts** - Team CRUD, ECIES-wrapped Per-Team Key hierarchy, CASL permissions
    73→- [ ] **Phase 20: Document Editors** - TipTap rich text and Univer spreadsheet editors with decrypt-edit-encrypt pipeline
    74→- [ ] **Phase 21: Document Signing** - ECDSA signing/verification, visual signature capture, multi-party workflows
    75→
    76→See `.planning/milestones/m3/ROADMAP.md` for full M3 phase details.
    77→
    78→## Phase Details
    79→
    80→### Phase 11: Cross-Platform Desktop
    81→
    82→**Goal**: CipherBox desktop app runs on Linux and Windows with native filesystem integration
    83→**Depends on**: Phase 9 (macOS desktop complete in M1). Can run in parallel with any M2 phase.
    84→**Requirements**: PLAT-01, PLAT-02
    85→**Research flag**: NEEDS `/gsd:research-phase` -- Linux FUSE (libfuse) and Windows virtual drive (WinFsp or Dokany) have platform-specific build and packaging requirements. Tauri cross-compilation and CI matrix need investigation.
    86→**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
    87→
    88→1. Linux user can install CipherBox via AppImage or .deb, log in, and access a FUSE mount at ~/CipherBox
    89→2. Windows user can install CipherBox via MSI or NSIS installer, log in, and access a virtual drive (e.g., C:\CipherBox or mapped drive letter)
    90→3. Background sync, system tray, and keychain storage work on both platforms (parity with macOS)
    91→4. CI builds and packages desktop apps for all three platforms (macOS, Linux, Windows)
    92→   **Plans**: TBD
    93→
    94→### Phase 12: Core Kit Identity Provider Foundation
    95→
    96→**Goal**: Replace PnP Modal SDK with MPC Core Kit and establish CipherBox backend as the identity provider for Web3Auth, building the foundation for MFA, SIWE, and cross-device approval in subsequent phases
    97→**Depends on**: Phase 10 (Milestone 1 complete)
    98→**Requirements**: MFA-01 (partial — foundation only), AUTH infrastructure
    99→**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
   100→
   101→1. User can log in via Google OAuth through CipherBox-branded UI (not Web3Auth modal)
   102→2. User can log in via email through CipherBox-branded UI
   103→3. CipherBox backend issues JWTs with `sub = userId`, verified by Web3Auth custom verifier
   104→4. Core Kit initialization, login, and private key export work end-to-end
   105→5. Existing PnP users' keys are preserved via `importTssKey` migration
   106→6. User's derived keypair (publicKey) remains identical after migration — vault data stays accessible
   107→
   108→**Plans:** 5 plans
   109→
   110→Plans:
   111→
   112→- [ ] 12-PLAN-01.md — Backend identity provider (JWKS, Google OAuth, email OTP, JWT issuing)
   113→- [ ] 12-PLAN-02.md — Core Kit SDK installation + React context provider
   114→- [ ] 12-PLAN-03.md — Frontend auth flow rewrite (loginWithJWT, key export, session)
   115→- [ ] 12-PLAN-04.md — Custom CipherBox-branded login UI (Google + email)
   116→- [ ] 12-PLAN-05.md — PnP migration (importTssKey), cleanup, and E2E verification
   117→
   118→### Phase 12.1: AES-CTR Streaming Encryption (INSERTED)
   119→
   120→**Goal**: Media files (video/audio) are encrypted with AES-256-CTR instead of GCM, enabling byte-range decryption for in-browser streaming playback via Service Worker transparent decrypt proxy
   121→**Depends on**: Phase 12.6 (per-file IPNS metadata with encryptionMode field)
   122→**Requirements**: Spec'd in TECHNICAL_ARCHITECTURE.md (v1.1 roadmap item), DATA_FLOWS.md (CTR upload/download sequences)
   123→**Research flag**: COMPLETE -- Service Worker decrypt proxy pattern, CTR nonce/counter management, streaming upload pipeline, IPFS byte-range limitations researched
   124→**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
   125→
   126→1. Media files (detected by MIME type + size threshold) are encrypted with AES-256-CTR; all other files continue using AES-256-GCM
   127→2. User can play encrypted video/audio in-browser without downloading the entire file first (streaming decryption via Service Worker)
   128→3. Upload pipeline streams file data through CTR encryption instead of loading entirely into memory
   129→4. Custom player UI with decrypt progress bar, buffering state, and CipherBox branding
   130→5. encryptionMode field in metadata drives mode selection (CTR for media, GCM default)
   131→
   132→**Plans:** 4 plans
   133→
   134→Plans:
   135→
   136→- [x] 12.1-01-PLAN.md — CTR crypto primitives: encryptAesCtr, decryptAesCtr, decryptAesCtrRange, generateCtrIv, constants, tests
   137→- [x] 12.1-02-PLAN.md — Streaming upload: mode selection (MIME + size), CTR streaming encrypt via TransformStream, mode-aware pipeline
   138→- [x] 12.1-03-PLAN.md — Service Worker: decrypt proxy (fetch intercept, CTR range decrypt, auth token, caching), registration, Vite build
   139→- [x] 12.1-04-PLAN.md — Integration: mode-aware download, useStreamingPreview hook, VideoPlayerDialog + AudioPlayerDialog with decrypt progress
   140→
   141→### Phase 12.2: Encrypted Device Registry (INSERTED)
   142→
   143→**Goal**: Encrypted device metadata stored on IPFS alongside user's vault, providing durable infrastructure for cross-device approval and resilience against backend rebuilds
   144→**Depends on**: Phase 12 (Core Kit foundation must be in place)
   145→**Requirements**: Infrastructure for MFA-02 (device management)
   146→**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
   147→
   148→1. Authenticated devices are tracked in an encrypted registry pinned on IPFS
   149→2. Device registry is encrypted with user's key and only readable by the user
   150→3. Device metadata includes public keys, device names, authorization status, and revocation capability
   151→4. Registry is discoverable and recoverable by any authenticated session
   152→
   153→**Plans:** 3 plans
   154→
   155→Plans:
   156→
   157→- [x] 12.2-PLAN-01.md — Registry and device crypto primitives (types, HKDF IPNS derivation, ECIES encrypt/decrypt, device keygen, tests)
   158→- [x] 12.2-PLAN-02.md — Device identity persistence (IndexedDB) and registry service (CRUD + IPFS/IPNS publish)
   159→- [x] 12.2-PLAN-03.md — Auth flow integration (Zustand store, non-blocking init, polling, logout cleanup)
   160→
   161→### Phase 12.3: SIWE + Unified Identity (INSERTED)
   162→
   163→**Goal**: Wallet users can log in via SIWE and all auth methods (wallet, Google, email) resolve to the same CipherBox identity and Web3Auth key
   164→**Depends on**: Phase 12.2 (device registry for multi-device state)
   165→**Requirements**: AUTH unification, MFA-01 (wallet MFA prerequisite)
   166→**Research flag**: COMPLETE -- SIWE message format, backend verification, wallet address hashing, multi-auth linking UX researched
   167→**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
   168→
   169→1. Wallet user can sign SIWE message -> CipherBox API verifies -> issues JWT -> Core Kit login succeeds
   170→2. User can link additional auth methods (second wallet, email) from settings
   171→3. Any linked auth method produces a JWT with same `sub = userId` -> same Web3Auth key
   172→4. Wallet addresses are stored as hashes in the database (not plaintext)
   173→5. ADR-001 legacy code (signatureKeyDerivation, derivationVersion, external_wallet) is fully removed (clean break, no migration needed)
   174→
   175→**Plans:** 4 plans
   176→
   177→Plans:
   178→
   179→- [x] 12.3-01-PLAN.md — Backend SIWE service, schema evolution, wallet identity endpoints
   180→- [x] 12.3-02-PLAN.md — Backend ADR-001 cleanup (auth service, vault export, verifier, API client regen)
   181→- [x] 12.3-03-PLAN.md — Frontend wallet login (wagmi, WalletLoginButton, SIWE flow) + ADR-001 cleanup (rename derivedKeypair to vaultKeypair)
   182→- [x] 12.3-04-PLAN.md — Settings page auth method management (view, link, unlink)
   183→
   184→### Phase 12.3.1: Pre-Wipe Identity Cleanup (INSERTED)
   185→
   186→**Goal**: Implement schema-level identity changes as clean breaks before database wipe, avoiding throwaway migration code: deterministic vault IPNS derivation, SHA-256 hashed identifiers for all auth methods, and removal of cross-method email auto-linking
   187→**Depends on**: Phase 12.3 (SIWE + unified identity complete)
   188→**Requirements**: Self-sovereign recovery infrastructure, privacy-preserving auth storage
   189→**Research flag**: Skip — builds on established patterns (HKDF from Phase 12.2, SHA-256 hashing from Phase 12.3 wallet work)
   190→**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
   191→
   192→1. Vault IPNS keypair is derived deterministically from user's privateKey via HKDF (context: "cipherbox-vault-ipns-v1") — no random keygen, no backend dependency for vault discovery
   193→2. All auth method identifiers are stored as SHA-256 hashes: Google uses SHA-256(google_sub), email uses SHA-256(normalized_email), wallet uses SHA-256(checksummed_address)
   194→3. Each auth method (google, email, wallet) is an independent identity — no cross-method email auto-linking; users link methods explicitly via Settings
   195→4. Self-sovereign recovery path works: recovery phrase → privateKey → derive vault IPNS key → resolve IPNS → decrypt vault metadata
   196→5. TEE republishing continues to work — ipns.service.ts has no rootIpnsPublicKey dependency (passive compatibility, verified by grep)
   197→
   198→**Plans:** 4 plans
   199→
   200→Plans:
   201→
   202→- [x] 12.3.1-01-PLAN.md — Crypto: deterministic vault IPNS keypair derivation (HKDF) + updated initializeVault/encryptVaultKeys/decryptVaultKeys + EncryptedVaultKeys type cleanup + tests
   203→- [x] 12.3.1-02-PLAN.md — Backend: SHA-256 hashed identifiers for all auth methods + remove cross-method auto-linking
   204→- [x] 12.3.1-03-PLAN.md — Backend vault schema + frontend vault init for deterministic IPNS + API client regen
   205→- [x] 12.3.1-04-PLAN.md — Codebase-wide cleanup: desktop Rust, E2E helpers, controller spec rootIpnsPublicKey removal
   206→
   207→### Phase 12.4: MFA + Cross-Device Approval (INSERTED)
   208→
   209→**Goal**: Users can enroll in MFA with device shares and recovery phrases, and approve new devices from existing authenticated devices
   210→**Depends on**: Phase 12.3.1 (identity cleanup complete, deterministic IPNS for recovery)
   211→**Requirements**: MFA-01, MFA-02, MFA-03, MFA-04
   212→**Research flag**: COMPLETE -- Core Kit enableMFA() flow, factor management, bulletin board API, ECIES ephemeral key exchange researched
   213→**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
   214→
   215→1. User can enable MFA from settings and is guided through factor enrollment (device share + recovery phrase)
   216→2. User can approve a new device from an existing authenticated device (bulletin board pattern)
   217→3. User can recover access using recovery phrase when device share is lost
   218→4. User's derived keypair (publicKey) remains identical after MFA enrollment — vault data stays accessible
   219→5. MFA factors are manageable from settings (view, add, revoke)
   220→
   221→**Plans:** 5 plans
   222→
   223→Plans:
   224→
   225→- [x] 12.4-01-PLAN.md — Backend bulletin board API (DeviceApproval entity, service, controller, DTOs)
   226→- [x] 12.4-02-PLAN.md — MFA hooks + store + REQUIRED_SHARE login flow branching
   227→- [x] 12.4-03-PLAN.md — MFA enrollment wizard + Settings Security tab UI
   228→- [x] 12.4-04-PLAN.md — Cross-device approval flow (waiting screen, approval modal, recovery input, enrollment prompt)
   229→- [x] 12.4-05-PLAN.md — API client regen + integration verification + cleanup
   230→
   231→### Phase 12.5: MFA Polishing, UAT & E2E Testing (INSERTED)
   232→
   233→**Goal**: Fix bugs from CoreKit auth UAT, wire missing SecurityTab UI, add wallet E2E tests with `@johanneskares/wallet-mock` (EIP-6963 mock provider), and complete UAT for all auth + MFA flows
   234→**Depends on**: Phase 12.4 (MFA + Cross-Device Approval complete)
   235→**Requirements**: Quality gate before proceeding to new features
   236→**Research flag**: Skip — builds on existing E2E infrastructure and UAT findings from `.planning/debug/corekit-auth-uat.md`
   237→**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
   238→
   239→1. ISSUE-004 fixed: SecurityTab wired into SettingsPage with tab navigation (unblocks MFA enrollment/device management UI)
   240→2. Wallet E2E tests pass using `@johanneskares/wallet-mock` EIP-6963 mock provider — no real wallet extension required
   241→3. Wallet UAT complete: TC09 (happy path), TC10 (cancel), TC11 (no wallet), TC12 (reject signature) all PASS
   242→4. MFA UAT complete: TC15-23 (MFA login flows) and TC25-31 (enrollment, devices, recovery) all PASS or documented
   243→5. All bugs discovered during UAT are fixed and verified
   244→6. Auth-related E2E test suite runs reliably in CI without flakiness
   245→
   246→**Plans:** 3 plans
   247→
   248→Plans:
   249→
   250→- [x] 12.5-01-PLAN.md — Fix ISSUE-004: Wire SecurityTab into SettingsPage with ARIA tab navigation

   253→
   254→### Phase 12.6: Per-File IPNS Metadata Split (INSERTED)
   255→
   256→**Goal**: Split file metadata into separate per-file IPNS-addressed objects so content updates don't require folder republishes, and per-file sharing becomes possible
   257→**Depends on**: Phase 12.5 (MFA polish complete, clean-break window before vault wipe)
   258→**Requirements**: Foundation for SHARE-01 (per-file sharing), VER-01 (version history in file metadata), performance improvement for content updates
   259→**Research flag**: COMPLETE -- TEE republish scalability benchmarked, HKDF file keypair derivation designed, batch publish strategy defined, FUSE client impact deferred
   260→**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
   261→
   262→1. File metadata (CID, fileKeyEncrypted, fileIv, size, mimeType) lives in its own IPNS record, derived via HKDF from user privateKey + fileId
   263→2. Folder metadata contains only file name fields + fileMetaIpnsName pointer — no embedded CIDs or file keys
   264→3. Content update (re-upload) publishes only the file's IPNS record, not the parent folder's
   265→4. File rename publishes only the folder IPNS record, not the file's
   266→5. Batch operations (multi-file upload) publish all file IPNS records in a single API call (preserving Phase 7.1 atomicity)
   267→6. TEE republisher handles per-file IPNS records with acceptable scalability (defined during research)
   268→7. Desktop FUSE client reads per-file IPNS metadata correctly
   269→8. Vault export includes per-file metadata in portable format
   270→
   271→**Plans:** 5 plans

   277→- [x] 12.6-03-PLAN.md — Frontend services: file-metadata service, v2 folder.service.ts rewrite, download/delete flow updates, store types
   278→- [x] 12.6-04-PLAN.md — Frontend hooks + components: useFolder/useFilePreview/useDropUpload v2, FileBrowser/TextEditor/DetailsDialog updates

   282→
   283→**Goal**: Eliminate folder metadata v1/v2 dual-schema code -- make v2 (FilePointer) the only format, tighten validation to reject hybrid metadata, and implement per-file IPNS publishing in desktop FUSE
   284→**Depends on**: Phase 11.1 (macOS Desktop Catch-Up), Phase 12.6 (Per-File IPNS Metadata Split)
   285→**Requirements**: Data integrity, cross-device interop
   286→**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
   287→
   288→1. Only v2 folder metadata (FilePointer children with fileMetaIpnsName) is written by all clients
   289→2. v1 folder metadata (inline FileEntry with cid/fileKeyEncrypted) is rejected by validators on all platforms
   290→3. All v1/v2 branching code removed: ~500 lines of dual-schema types, dispatch, and conversion
   291→4. Desktop FUSE create() derives file IPNS keypair and release() publishes per-file FileMetadata
   292→5. Desktop build_folder_metadata emits FilePointer (not FileEntry) -- cross-device format is consistent
   293→6. TypeScript crypto package exports canonical names (FolderMetadata, FolderChild) -- no V2 suffix
   294→7. Recovery tool (recovery.html) handles only v2 FilePointer path
   295→8. All tests pass: pnpm test + cargo test --features fuse
   296→
   297→**Plans:** 3 plans
   298→
   299→Plans:
   300→
   301→- [x] 11.2-01-PLAN.md — TypeScript crypto types: delete v1, rename v2 to canonical, update web app imports
   302→- [x] 11.2-02-PLAN.md — Rust desktop: delete v1 types, rename v2, rewrite build_folder_metadata to FilePointer
   303→- [x] 11.2-03-PLAN.md — Per-file IPNS in FUSE create/release, recovery tool v2-only, cross-platform verification
   304→
   305→### Phase 13: File Versioning
   306→
   307→**Goal**: Users can access and restore previous versions of their files
   308→**Depends on**: Phase 12
   309→**Requirements**: VER-01, VER-02, VER-03, VER-04, VER-05
   310→**Research flag**: Standard patterns -- metadata schema extension plus "stop unpinning old CIDs." Skip `/gsd:research-phase`.
   311→**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
   312→
   313→1. When a user uploads a new version of an existing file, the previous version is automatically retained (old CID stays pinned)
   314→2. User can open a version history panel for any file and see a list of previous versions with timestamps
   315→3. User can restore a previous version, which becomes the current version while preserving the version chain
   316→4. Version retention policy is enforced (configurable max versions per file) and excess versions are pruned automatically
   317→5. Storage consumed by retained versions counts against the user's 500 MiB quota
   318→
   319→**Plans:** 5 plans
   320→
   321→Plans:
   322→
   323→- [x] 13-01-PLAN.md — Crypto types: VersionEntry type in TS + Rust, FileMetadata versions array, backward-compatible validator
   324→- [x] 13-02-PLAN.md — Web versioning logic: updateFileMetadata with version push/prune, cooldown, stop unpinning old CIDs
   325→- [x] 13-03-PLAN.md — Desktop FUSE versioning: release() version creation, 15-min cooldown, stop unpinning old CIDs
   326→- [x] 13-04-PLAN.md — Version history UI: DetailsDialog version panel, download/restore/delete past versions
   327→- [x] 13-05-PLAN.md — Recovery tool version support + full cross-platform build verification
   328→
   329→### Phase 14: User-to-User Sharing
   330→
   331→**Goal**: Users can share encrypted folders and individual files with other CipherBox users while maintaining zero-knowledge guarantees. Instant share via public key paste (no accept/decline flow). Read-only only. Lazy key rotation on revoke.
   332→**Depends on**: Phase 13
   333→**Requirements**: SHARE-01, SHARE-02, SHARE-03, SHARE-04, SHARE-05
   334→**Research flag**: COMPLETE -- ECIES re-wrapping protocol, share record architecture, lazy rotation protocol, recipient browsing architecture researched
   335→**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
   336→
   337→1. User can share a folder or file (read-only) with another CipherBox user by re-wrapping the folderKey/fileKey with the recipient's publicKey via ECIES
   338→2. User can paste a recipient's secp256k1 public key and the share takes effect instantly (no accept/decline)
   339→3. User can revoke a share, which triggers lazy folderKey rotation on the next folder modification
   340→4. Recipient can browse shared folders in a "Shared with me" section at ~/shared
   341→5. Server never sees plaintext folderKey or fileKey at any point during the sharing flow
   342→
   343→**Plans:** 6 plans
   344→
   345→Plans:
   346→
   347→- [x] 14-01-PLAN.md — Crypto reWrapKey utility + Share/ShareKey TypeORM entities
   348→- [x] 14-02-PLAN.md — Backend shares module (service, controller, 8 endpoints, DTOs) + API client regen
   349→- [x] 14-03-PLAN.md — Frontend share store + share service + Settings public key display
   350→- [x] 14-04-PLAN.md — ShareDialog modal + context menu Share action + FileBrowser wiring
   351→- [x] 14-05-PLAN.md — "Shared with me" browsing (route, SharedFileBrowser, read-only enforcement, shared download)
   352→- [x] 14-06-PLAN.md — Post-upload share key propagation + revocation + lazy key rotation
   353→
   354→### Phase 15: Link Sharing
   355→
   356→**Goal**: Users can share files and folders via invite links where the decryption key lives in the URL fragment only (never sent to server). Recipients must authenticate (invite model) and the share is auto-claimed using Phase 14 infrastructure.
   357→**Depends on**: Phase 14
   358→**Requirements**: SHARE-06, SHARE-07
   359→**Research flag**: COMPLETE -- ephemeral key bridge pattern, HashRouter fragment handling, unauthenticated endpoint design researched
   360→**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
   361→
   362→1. User can generate a shareable link for a file where the decryption key is in the URL fragment only (never sent to server)
   363→2. Recipient can open the link, log in or create an account, and the share is auto-claimed (appears in "Shared with me")
   364→
   365→**Plans:** 3 plans

   368→
   369→- [ ] 15-01-PLAN.md — Backend: ShareInvite entity, migration, DTOs, InvitesController, service methods, module registration
   370→- [ ] 15-02-PLAN.md — API client regen + frontend invite service with ephemeral key bridge crypto
   371→- [ ] 15-03-PLAN.md — ShareDialog tabbed UI (Direct Share | Invite Link) + InvitePage landing page + route + build verification
   372→
   373→### Phase 15.1: Client-Side Search (INSERTED)
   374→
   375→**Goal**: Users can search file names across their entire vault with an encrypted index persisted in IndexedDB
   376→**Depends on**: Phase 15
   377→**Requirements**: SRCH-01, SRCH-02, SRCH-03
   378→**Research flag**: Standard patterns -- minisearch + idb (per research), skip `/gsd:research-phase`
   379→**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
   380→
   381→1. User can search file names across all folders and see matching results with navigation to the file location
   382→2. Search index is encrypted and persisted in IndexedDB, surviving page refreshes
   383→3. Search index updates incrementally when IPNS polling detects metadata changes
   384→   **Plans**: TBD
   385→
   386→### Phase 16: Advanced Sync
   387→
   388→**Goal**: Users experience reliable sync with conflict awareness and offline resilience
   389→**Depends on**: Phase 15
   390→**Requirements**: SYNC-04, SYNC-05, SYNC-06
   391→**Research flag**: NEEDS `/gsd:research-phase` -- three-way merge edge cases with encrypted metadata need exhaustive test matrix. Offline replay with idempotency keys is uncharted territory for this codebase.
   392→**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
   393→
   394→1. Client detects when another device has published a newer IPNS sequence number and alerts the user before overwriting
   395→2. When the user goes offline and makes changes, operations are queued locally and automatically replayed on reconnect
   396→3. Queued operations use idempotency keys so replaying them after reconnect never produces duplicate files or folders
   397→   **Plans**: TBD
   398→
   399→### Phase 17: AWS Nitro TEE

   401→**Goal**: IPNS republishing has a fallback TEE provider for high availability
   402→**Depends on**: Phase 12 (can run in parallel with Phases 14-16 after MFA stabilizes auth)

   407→1. AWS Nitro enclave can receive ECIES-encrypted IPNS keys, decrypt in hardware, sign IPNS records, and zero memory

   409→   **Plans**: TBD

1→# CipherBox
     2→
     3→## What This Is
     4→
     5→CipherBox is an ambitious demonstration of privacy-first encrypted cloud storage using IPFS/IPNS and Web3Auth. It provides zero-knowledge file storage where the server never has access to plaintext files or encryption keys. The platform targets developers and privacy-conscious users who want encrypted storage with sharing, search, and multi-factor authentication.
     6→
     7→## Core Value
     8→
     9→**Zero-knowledge privacy**: Files are encrypted client-side before leaving the device, and encryption keys exist only in client memory. The server is cryptographically unable to access user data.
    10→
    11→## Current Milestone: v1.0 Production-Grade Storage
    12→
    13→**Goal:** Elevate the staging MVP into a production-ready encrypted storage platform with sharing, search, MFA, file versioning, and cross-platform desktop support.
    14→
    15→**Target features:**
    16→
    17→- File/folder sharing with encrypted key exchange (user-to-user)
    18→- Client-side encrypted search index
    19→- Multi-factor authentication (passkey, TOTP, recovery phrase)
    20→- File version history with restore
    21→- Advanced sync (conflict resolution, offline queue, selective sync)
    22→- Cross-platform desktop apps (Linux and Windows, extending macOS from M1)
    23→- AWS Nitro TEE as fallback republishing provider
    24→
    25→## Requirements
    26→
    27→### Validated (Milestone 1 — Staging MVP)
    28→
    29→- Web3Auth authentication (email, OAuth, magic link, external wallet) — M1
    30→- Client-side AES-256-GCM encryption + ECIES key wrapping — M1
    31→- IPFS file storage via Pinata with IPNS metadata — M1
    32→- Full file/folder CRUD with 20-level hierarchy — M1
    33→- File browser web UI with terminal aesthetic — M1
    34→- Multi-device sync via IPNS polling (30s) — M1
    35→- TEE auto-republishing via Phala Cloud — M1
    36→- macOS desktop client with Tauri + FUSE mount — M1
    37→- Vault export with standalone recovery tool — M1
    38→- CI/CD pipeline with staging deployment — M1
    39→
    40→### Active (Milestone 2 — Production v1.0)
    41→
    42→#### File Sharing
    43→
    44→- [ ] User can share files/folders with other CipherBox users
    45→- [ ] User can generate shareable link for file
    46→- [ ] User can set password on shared link
    47→- [ ] User can set expiration on shared link
    48→- [ ] Recipient can download shared file without CipherBox account
    49→
    50→#### Search
    51→
    52→- [ ] User can search file names across vault
    53→- [ ] Search index is encrypted client-side
    54→
    55→#### Multi-Factor Authentication
    56→
    57→- [ ] User can enable MFA in settings
    58→- [ ] User can enroll passkey/WebAuthn as second factor
    59→- [ ] User can enroll TOTP authenticator as second factor
    60→- [ ] User can generate recovery phrase for account recovery
    61→
    62→#### File Versioning
    63→
    64→- [ ] System keeps previous versions of files
    65→- [ ] User can view version history
    66→- [ ] User can restore previous version
    67→
    68→#### Advanced Sync
    69→
    70→- [ ] Conflict detection with user resolution UI
    71→- [ ] Offline write queue with retry on reconnect
    72→- [ ] Selective sync (choose folders to sync locally)
    73→
    74→#### TEE Enhancements
    75→
    76→- [ ] AWS Nitro as fallback TEE provider
    77→
    78→### Out of Scope (Milestone 2)
    79→
    80→- Billing/payments — deferred to Milestone 3
    81→- Docs/sheets/slides editors — deferred to Milestone 3
    82→- Team accounts / org structure — deferred to Milestone 3
    83→- Secure document signing — deferred to Milestone 3
    84→- Mobile apps (iOS/Android) — deferred to Milestone 3+
    85→- Linux/Windows desktop — moved to Milestone 2 (Phase 11)
    86→- Collaborative editing — deferred to Milestone 3+
    87→- AES-256-CTR streaming encryption — moved to M2 Phase 12.1
    88→
    89→## Context
    90→
    91→**Existing Codebase:**
    92→
    93→- Complete specifications in `00-Preliminary-R&D/Documentation/` (PRD, API spec, technical architecture, data flows, client spec, implementation roadmap)
    94→- Working PoC console harness in `00-Preliminary-R&D/poc/` that validates IPFS/IPNS and encryption flows
    95→- Codebase mapping in `.planning/codebase/`
    96→
    97→**Technical Environment:**
    98→
    99→- IPFS via Pinata for file storage and pinning
   100→- IPNS for mutable metadata pointers
   101→- Web3Auth for deterministic ECDSA key derivation
   102→- Phala Cloud (primary) / AWS Nitro (fallback) for TEE republishing
   103→
   104→**Key Architecture Decisions (from specs):**
   105→
   106→- Client-side encryption only — server is zero-knowledge relay
   107→- Per-folder IPNS keypairs — enables future modular sharing
   108→- Backend relays signed IPNS records — never holds signing keys
   109→- TEE receives ECIES-encrypted IPNS keys — decrypts in hardware only
   110→
   111→## Constraints
   112→
   113→- **File size**: 100 MB max — browser memory limits
   114→- **Storage quota**: 500 MiB free tier — Pinata cost management
   115→- **Files per folder**: 1,000 max — UI performance
   116→- **Folder depth**: 20 levels max — traversal performance
   117→- **Sync latency**: ~30 seconds — IPNS polling interval
   118→- **Tech stack**: NestJS backend, React 18 frontend, Tauri desktop — per specifications
   119→- **Auth provider**: Web3Auth only — deterministic key derivation requirement
   120→- **IPFS provider**: Pinata — managed pinning service
   121→
   122→## Key Decisions
   123→
   124→| Decision                           | Rationale                                 | Outcome   |
   125→| ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | --------- |
   126→| Full-stack vertical build order    | Test features end-to-end as they're built | — Pending |
   127→| Web + macOS desktop for v1.0       | Complete user experience across platforms | — Pending |
   128→| TEE republishing required for v1.0 | Zero-downtime vault access guarantee      | — Pending |
   129→| Implement specs as documented      | Specs are finalized and comprehensive     | — Pending |
   130→
   131→---
   132→
   133→Last updated: 2026-02-11 after Milestone 2 initialization
   134→

1→# Phase 15: Link Sharing - Context
     2→
     3→**Gathered:** 2026-02-23
     4→**Status:** Ready for planning
     5→
     6→<domain>
     7→## Phase Boundary
     8→
     9→Share files and folders via invite links. Recipients click the link, log in (or create an account), and the share is auto-claimed using Phase 14's ECIES re-wrapping infrastructure. This is an **invite model** (account required), NOT an unauthenticated web viewer.
    10→
    11→Scope: invite link generation, ephemeral key bridge, claim flow, landing page, Share dialog updates, link management (view active, revoke).
    12→
    13→Out of scope: unauthenticated file viewing, password-protected links, multi-claim links, short domains.
    14→
    15→</domain>
    16→
    17→<decisions>
    18→## Implementation Decisions
    19→
    20→### Sharing model
    21→
    22→- **Invite link model** (account required) -- not unauthenticated access
    23→- Link = invitation to claim a share; recipient must log in or sign up
    24→- Serves as user acquisition funnel -- new users can sign up through the invite flow
    25→- After claim, share appears in recipient's "Shared with me" (Phase 14 infrastructure)
    26→
    27→### Ephemeral key bridge
    28→
    29→- Core challenge: ECIES needs recipient's public key, but recipient may not exist yet
    30→- Solution: sharer generates ephemeral secp256k1 keypair
    31→- Wraps file/folder key with ephemeral public key, stores wrapped ciphertext on server
    32→- Ephemeral PRIVATE key goes in URL fragment (never sent to server -- zero-knowledge preserved)
    33→- Recipient claims: uses ephemeral key to unwrap, re-wraps with their own public key
    34→- Creates standard Phase 14 Share + ShareKey records
    35→- Well-established pattern (Signal invite links, Bitwarden Send)
    36→
    37→### Invite landing page
    38→
    39→- New route: `/invite/:token#ephemeralPrivateKey`
    40→- Branded but opaque -- CipherBox branding + "Someone shared a file with you"
    41→- Do NOT reveal file name or sharer identity before auth
    42→- Prominent login/signup CTA button
    43→- After auth, share is auto-claimed and recipient navigates directly to the shared content
    44→- Error states: expired (7-day TTL), already claimed, revoked -- all show friendly error card with red border
    45→
    46→### Link generation flow
    47→
    48→- Lives in existing ShareDialog as a new tab alongside "Direct Share" (paste pubkey)
    49→- Tab bar: DIRECT SHARE | INVITE LINK (2px green bottom-border active indicator)
    50→- "Create invite link" primary button in invite tab
    51→- Shows active (unclaimed, unexpired) links with --copy and --revoke actions
    52→- Links auto-copied to clipboard on creation
    53→- Modal widened from 500px to 600px to accommodate tab bar
    54→
    55→### Link lifecycle
    56→
    57→- Default expiry: 7 days (configurable constant, easy to change later)
    58→- Single-claim: first person to claim gets it (maxClaims=1, extensible to multi-claim later)
    59→- Revoking invite link only prevents new claims -- already-claimed shares persist independently
    60→- Auto-cleanup on read: expired records deleted when querying invites (same pattern as device approval Phase 12.4)
    61→- No rate limiting on link creation
    62→
    63→### Data architecture
    64→
    65→- New ShareInvite database table (not IPFS) -- ephemeral, short-lived data
    66→- Stores: invite token, wrapped key ciphertext, item reference (ipnsName), sharer userId, expiry, status, claimedBy
    67→- Invite token: URL-safe base64, ~22 chars, 128 bits of entropy
    68→- URL on main app domain: `app.cipherbox.cc/invite/:token#ephemeralKey`
    69→- Claiming auto-creates Phase 14 Share + ShareKey records -- recipient sees it in "Shared with me"
    70→
    71→### Claude's Discretion
    72→
    73→- Exact invite token generation implementation
    74→- Database cleanup query strategy (batch vs per-request)
    75→- Error page illustrations/copy refinement
    76→- Clipboard copy UX feedback (toast, animation, etc.)
    77→
    78→</decisions>
    79→
    80→<specifics>
    81→## Specific Ideas
    82→
    83→- "I want to use the share feature as a funnel to get users to create accounts" -- landing page should encourage sign-up
    84→- Start branded-but-opaque (no info before auth), can A/B test showing file name later
    85→- Direct-to-content navigation after claim preferred over redirect to "Shared with me" list
    86→- Auto-cleanup preferred over audit trail -- can switch to keeping records later if users want history
    87→
    88→</specifics>
    89→
    90→<deferred>
    91→## Deferred Ideas
    92→
    93→- Password-protected invite links (ephemeral key + password double layer) -- future enhancement
    94→- Multi-claim links (share with N recipients from one link) -- maxClaims column ready, just needs UI
    95→- Short domain for cleaner URLs (cb.link/) -- requires DNS/redirect infrastructure
    96→- Unauthenticated web viewer (key-in-fragment, no account needed) -- fundamentally different security surface, could be its own phase
    97→- Client-side search -- split into Phase 15.1
    98→
    99→</deferred>
   100→
   101→## Approved Design Direction
   102→
   103→**Screens in Pencil:**
   104→
   105→- `P15 - Invite Landing (Valid)` -- full-page centered card, CipherBox branding, login CTA
   106→- `P15 - Invite Landing (Expired)` -- red border error card, expiry message, --home button
   107→- `P15 - Share Dialog (Invite Tab)` -- tabbed modal with invite link management
   108→
   109→**Key design patterns:**
   110→
   111→- Tab bar: 2px bottom-border active indicator, green/muted color states
   112→- Status badges: ACTIVE (green border), inline with link metadata
   113→- Invite landing: full-viewport centered card (no sidebar), mirrors Phase 12.4 new-device-waiting pattern
   114→- Error states: red (#EF4444) border on card, matching existing error pattern
   115→
   116→---
   117→
   118→_Phase: 15-link-sharing_
   119→_Context gathered: 2026-02-23_
   120→

1→# Phase 15: Link Sharing - Research
     2→
     3→**Researched:** 2026-02-23
     4→**Domain:** Invite link sharing with ephemeral key bridge, ECIES cryptography, NestJS API, React SPA
     5→**Confidence:** HIGH
     6→
     7→## Summary
     8→
     9→Phase 15 adds invite link sharing to CipherBox, building on the Phase 14 user-to-user sharing infrastructure. The core innovation is an "ephemeral key bridge" -- the sharer generates a temporary secp256k1 keypair, wraps the file/folder key with the ephemeral public key, and puts the ephemeral private key in the URL fragment. When the recipient authenticates and claims the invite, they use the ephemeral private key to unwrap the key, then re-wrap it with their own public key, creating standard Phase 14 Share + ShareKey records.
    10→
    11→The existing codebase provides all necessary cryptographic primitives (`wrapKey`, `unwrapKey` from `@cipherbox/crypto`), the Phase 14 Share/ShareKey entities and service, the ShareDialog component, and the Orval-generated API client. The primary work is: (1) a new `ShareInvite` entity/migration, (2) new API endpoints for invite CRUD + claim, (3) an invite landing page route, (4) ShareDialog tabbed interface, and (5) the ephemeral key generation + claim crypto flow.
    12→
    13→**Primary recommendation:** Extend the existing `SharesModule` with invite endpoints rather than creating a new module. The invite system is tightly coupled to share creation and should reuse `SharesService.createShare()` during the claim flow.
    14→
    15→## Critical Discovery: HashRouter Fragment Collision
    16→
    17→**Confidence: HIGH** (verified by reading `apps/web/src/routes/index.tsx`)
    18→
    19→The app uses `HashRouter` from react-router-dom, meaning ALL routes are already in the URL fragment (`/#/path`). The planned URL format `app.cipherbox.cc/invite/:token#ephemeralKey` is **incompatible** with HashRouter -- there is only one `#` in a URL.
    20→
    21→### Solution Options (ranked)
    22→
    23→1. **Encode ephemeral key as query parameter within the hash route:** `/#/invite/:token?key=<ephemeralPrivateKeyHex>` -- The "query string" lives within the hash fragment so it is never sent to the server. React Router parses this via `useSearchParams()`. This is the simplest approach and maintains zero-knowledge since everything after `#` stays client-side.
    24→
    25→2. **Use a path segment:** `/#/invite/:token/:ephemeralPrivateKeyHex` -- Simpler parsing but the key is visible in the route definition. Also never sent to server (still within hash).
    26→
    27→3. **Switch to BrowserRouter for the invite route only** -- Extremely complex, requires server-side redirect config, not recommended.
    28→
    29→**Recommendation: Option 1** -- `/#/invite/:token?key=<hex>`. The entire string after `#` is the hash fragment and is never sent to the server in HTTP requests. React Router's `useSearchParams()` works within HashRouter. This preserves the zero-knowledge property while being simple to implement.
    30→
    31→**Security note:** The `?key=...` part is WITHIN the hash fragment (`#/invite/TOKEN?key=KEY`), so it is NOT a real URL query parameter. It never hits the server. Browsers do not send anything after `#` in HTTP requests.
    32→
    33→## Standard Stack
    34→
    35→### Core (already in codebase)
    36→
    37→| Library                       | Version                         | Purpose                                          | Location                        |
    38→| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------- |
    39→| `@cipherbox/crypto` (eciesjs) | 0.4.16                          | ECIES wrapKey/unwrapKey for ephemeral key bridge | `packages/crypto/src/ecies/`    |
    40→| `@noble/secp256k1`            | 3.0.0 (web), 2.2.3 (crypto pkg) | Ephemeral keypair generation                     | `apps/web/package.json`         |
    41→| TypeORM                       | (existing)                      | ShareInvite entity + migration                   | `apps/api/src/shares/`          |
    42→| NestJS                        | (existing)                      | Controller/service for invite endpoints          | `apps/api/src/shares/`          |
    43→| React Router (HashRouter)     | (existing)                      | `/invite/:token` route                           | `apps/web/src/routes/index.tsx` |
    44→| Orval                         | 7.18.0                          | API client generation                            | `apps/web/orval.config.ts`      |
    45→
    46→### No New Dependencies Required
    47→
    48→All cryptographic operations use existing primitives:
    49→
    50→- `wrapKey(plainKey, ephemeralPubKey)` -- wrap with ephemeral public key
    51→- `unwrapKey(wrappedKey, ephemeralPrivKey)` -- unwrap with ephemeral private key (from URL)
    52→- `wrapKey(plainKey, recipientPubKey)` -- re-wrap with recipient's own public key
    53→- `secp256k1.utils.randomPrivateKey()` -- generate ephemeral private key
    54→- `secp256k1.getPublicKey(privKey, false)` -- derive uncompressed public key
    55→
    56→## Architecture Patterns
    57→
    58→### Recommended Project Structure
    59→
    60→```
    61→apps/api/src/shares/
    62→  entities/
    63→    share.entity.ts          # (existing)
    64→    share-key.entity.ts       # (existing)
    65→    share-invite.entity.ts    # NEW
    66→    index.ts                  # UPDATE: export ShareInvite
    67→  dto/
    68→    create-invite.dto.ts      # NEW
    69→    claim-invite.dto.ts       # NEW
    70→    invite-response.dto.ts    # NEW
    71→  shares.controller.ts        # UPDATE: add invite endpoints
    72→  shares.service.ts           # UPDATE: add invite methods
    73→  shares.module.ts            # UPDATE: register ShareInvite entity
    74→
    75→apps/api/src/migrations/
    76→  1740400000000-AddShareInvites.ts  # NEW
    77→
    78→apps/web/src/
    79→  routes/
    80→    index.tsx                 # UPDATE: add /invite/:token route
    81→    InvitePage.tsx             # NEW: invite landing page
    82→  components/file-browser/
    83→    ShareDialog.tsx            # UPDATE: add tabbed interface
    84→    InviteLinkTab.tsx          # NEW: invite link tab content
    85→  services/
    86→    share.service.ts           # UPDATE: add invite service functions
    87→    invite.service.ts          # NEW: or extend share.service.ts
    88→  styles/
    89→    share-dialog.css           # UPDATE: add tab styles
    90→    invite-page.css            # NEW: invite landing page styles
    91→```
    92→
    93→### Pattern 1: ShareInvite Entity
    94→
    95→**What:** New database entity for ephemeral invite links
    96→**When to use:** Storing invite metadata that links sharer to wrapped key ciphertext
    97→
    98→```typescript
    99→// Source: Modeled after device-approval.entity.ts (auto-expire pattern) + share.entity.ts
   100→@Entity('share_invites')
   101→export class ShareInvite {
   102→  @PrimaryGeneratedColumn('uuid')
   103→  id!: string;
   104→
   105→  @Index({ unique: true })
   106→  @Column({ type: 'varchar', length: 44, name: 'token' })
   107→  token!: string; // URL-safe base64, ~22 chars (128 bits entropy)
   108→
   109→  @Column({ type: 'uuid', name: 'sharer_id' })
   110→  sharerId!: string;
   111→
   112→  @ManyToOne(() => User, { onDelete: 'CASCADE' })
   113→  @JoinColumn({ name: 'sharer_id' })
   114→  sharer!: User;
   115→
   116→  @Column({ type: 'varchar', length: 10, name: 'item_type' })
   117→  itemType!: 'folder' | 'file';
   118→
   119→  @Column({ type: 'varchar', length: 255, name: 'ipns_name' })
   120→  ipnsName!: string;
   121→
   122→  @Column({ type: 'varchar', length: 255, name: 'item_name' })
   123→  itemName!: string;
   124→
   125→  // The item key wrapped with the EPHEMERAL public key (not recipient's key)
   126→  @Column({ type: 'bytea', name: 'encrypted_key' })
   127→  encryptedKey!: Buffer;
   128→
   129→  // Child keys (subfolder/file keys) wrapped with ephemeral public key
   130→  // Stored as JSON array for simplicity (not a separate table)
   131→  @Column({ type: 'jsonb', name: 'encrypted_child_keys', nullable: true })
   132→  encryptedChildKeys!: Array<{
   133→    keyType: 'file' | 'folder';
   134→    itemId: string;
   135→    encryptedKey: string; // hex
   136→  }> | null;
   137→
   138→  @Column({ type: 'varchar', length: 20, default: 'active' })
   139→  status!: 'active' | 'claimed' | 'revoked';
   140→
   141→  @Column({ type: 'integer', name: 'max_claims', default: 1 })
   142→  maxClaims!: number;
   143→
   144→  @Column({ type: 'integer', name: 'claim_count', default: 0 })
   145→  claimCount!: number;
   146→
   147→  @Column({ type: 'uuid', name: 'claimed_by', nullable: true })
   148→  claimedBy!: string | null;
   149→
   150→  @Column({ type: 'timestamp', name: 'expires_at' })
   151→  expiresAt!: Date;
   152→
   153→  @CreateDateColumn({ name: 'created_at' })
   154→  createdAt!: Date;
   155→}
   156→```
   157→
   158→### Pattern 2: Auto-Expire on Read (Phase 12.4 Pattern)
   159→
   160→**What:** Delete expired records when querying, not via cron job
   161→**When to use:** TTL-based cleanup for short-lived records
   162→
   163→```typescript
   164→// Source: apps/api/src/device-approval/device-approval.service.ts lines 72-76
   165→// Pattern: check expiry when reading, update status inline
   166→async getInvite(token: string): Promise<ShareInvite | null> {
   167→  const invite = await this.inviteRepo.findOne({ where: { token } });
   168→  if (!invite) return null;
   169→
   170→  // Auto-expire if past TTL
   171→  if (invite.status === 'active' && invite.expiresAt < new Date()) {
   172→    await this.inviteRepo.remove(invite); // hard delete (not soft delete like device approvals)
   173→    return null;
   174→  }
   175→  return invite;
   176→}
   177→```
   178→
   179→### Pattern 3: Ephemeral Key Bridge (Claim Flow)
   180→
   181→**What:** The core cryptographic flow for claiming an invite link
   182→**When to use:** When recipient authenticates and claims the invite
   183→
   184→```typescript
   185→// Client-side claim flow (runs in browser after auth)
   186→async function claimInvite(token: string, ephemeralPrivKeyHex: string): Promise<void> {
   187→  // 1. Fetch invite metadata from server
   188→  const invite = await fetchInviteByToken(token);
   189→
   190→  // 2. Get recipient's own vault keypair
   191→  const vaultKeypair = useAuthStore.getState().vaultKeypair;
   192→  const ephemeralPrivKey = hexToBytes(ephemeralPrivKeyHex);
   193→
   194→  // 3. Unwrap the key using ephemeral private key
   195→  const plaintextKey = await unwrapKey(hexToBytes(invite.encryptedKey), ephemeralPrivKey);
   196→
   197→  // 4. Re-wrap with recipient's own public key
   198→  const reWrappedKey = await wrapKey(plaintextKey, vaultKeypair.publicKey);
   199→  plaintextKey.fill(0); // zero sensitive data
   200→
   201→  // 5. Re-wrap child keys similarly
   202→  const childKeys = [];
   203→  for (const ck of invite.encryptedChildKeys ?? []) {
   204→    const plainChildKey = await unwrapKey(hexToBytes(ck.encryptedKey), ephemeralPrivKey);
   205→    const reWrapped = await wrapKey(plainChildKey, vaultKeypair.publicKey);
   206→    plainChildKey.fill(0);
   207→    childKeys.push({
   208→      keyType: ck.keyType,
   209→      itemId: ck.itemId,
   210→      encryptedKey: bytesToHex(reWrapped),
   211→    });
   212→  }
   213→
   214→  // 6. Zero ephemeral key from memory
   215→  ephemeralPrivKey.fill(0);
   216→
   217→  // 7. Send claim to server (creates Share + ShareKey records via Phase 14 infra)
   218→  await claimInviteApi(token, {
   219→    encryptedKey: bytesToHex(reWrappedKey),
   220→    childKeys,
   221→  });
   222→}
   223→```
   224→
   225→### Pattern 4: Invite Token Generation
   226→
   227→**What:** Generate URL-safe tokens with 128 bits of entropy
   228→**When to use:** Creating invite links
   229→
   230→```typescript
   231→// Server-side token generation
   232→import { randomBytes } from 'crypto';
   233→
   234→function generateInviteToken(): string {
   235→  // 16 bytes = 128 bits of entropy
   236→  // URL-safe base64: ~22 chars
   237→  return randomBytes(16).toString('base64url');
   238→}
   239→```
   240→
   241→### Anti-Patterns to Avoid
   242→
   243→- **Storing ephemeral private key on server:** The entire point of the ephemeral key bridge is that the server never sees the ephemeral private key. It lives only in the URL fragment.
   244→- **Using a new NestJS module for invites:** Invites are tightly coupled to shares. Keep them in `SharesModule` to reuse `SharesService.createShare()` during claim.
   245→- **Creating a separate table for invite child keys:** Use JSONB column on the invite table -- invites are short-lived (7 days) and child keys are deleted with the invite on claim. No need for normalized storage.
   246→- **Omitting CREATE TABLE migration:** Per learnings from Phase 14 staging deployment, ALWAYS create a migration file. `synchronize: true` in dev hides missing migrations.
   247→
   248→## Don't Hand-Roll
   249→
   250→| Problem                      | Don't Build                           | Use Instead                                                      | Why                                                                    |
   251→| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   252→| ECIES key wrapping           | Custom ECDH + AES                     | `wrapKey`/`unwrapKey` from `@cipherbox/crypto`                   | Already handles ephemeral keys, HKDF, AES-GCM internally via `eciesjs` |
   253→| secp256k1 keypair generation | Web Crypto or manual curve ops        | `@noble/secp256k1` `utils.randomPrivateKey()` + `getPublicKey()` | Already used in `apps/web/src/lib/web3auth/hooks.ts:86`                |
   254→| URL-safe random tokens       | UUID or custom RNG                    | Node.js `crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('base64url')`           | Proper entropy, URL-safe encoding built-in                             |
   255→| Share creation after claim   | Duplicate share creation logic        | Call `SharesService.createShare()` internally                    | Reuses validation, duplicate detection, key storage                    |
   256→| API client types             | Manual fetch calls                    | `pnpm api:generate` (Orval)                                      | Maintains type safety, auto-generates from OpenAPI spec                |
   257→| Clipboard API                | Manual `document.execCommand('copy')` | `navigator.clipboard.writeText()`                                | Modern API, already in secure context (HTTPS)                          |
   258→
   259→## Common Pitfalls
   260→
   261→### Pitfall 1: HashRouter Fragment Collision
   262→
   263→**What goes wrong:** URL format `app.cipherbox.cc/invite/:token#ephemeralKey` fails because HashRouter uses `#` for routing. The entire path after `#` is the hash route.
   264→**Why it happens:** The app uses `HashRouter` (confirmed in `apps/web/src/routes/index.tsx:9`), not `BrowserRouter`.
   265→**How to avoid:** Use `/#/invite/:token?key=<ephemeralPrivKeyHex>` format. The `?key=` portion is within the hash fragment and parsed by React Router's `useSearchParams()`.
   266→**Warning signs:** URL parsing returns undefined for the ephemeral key, or the route doesn't match.
   267→
   268→### Pitfall 2: Missing CREATE TABLE Migration
   269→
   270→**What goes wrong:** ShareInvite table doesn't exist in staging/production, migration that modifies it fails.
   271→**Why it happens:** `synchronize: true` in dev auto-creates tables from entities, hiding the missing migration. Only fails when `synchronize: false` in staging/production.
   272→**How to avoid:** ALWAYS create a migration file with `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` for new entities. Use timestamp BEFORE any migration that modifies the table.
   273→**Warning signs:** Staging deployment fails with "relation does not exist" error.
   274→**Reference:** `.learnings/2026-02-22-staging-migration-missing-create-table.md`
   275→
   276→### Pitfall 3: Entity Registration in AppModule
   277→
   278→**What goes wrong:** TypeORM doesn't recognize the new entity, queries fail at runtime.
   279→**Why it happens:** New entity must be added to BOTH the module's `TypeOrmModule.forFeature()` AND the `entities` array in `app.module.ts`.

   285→### Pitfall 4: Ephemeral Key Memory Leaks
   286→
   287→**What goes wrong:** Ephemeral private key stays in memory after claim, potential security risk.
   288→**Why it happens:** Key is parsed from URL into a Uint8Array but never zeroed after use.
   289→**How to avoid:** Always `.fill(0)` ephemeral key material in a `finally` block after claim completes. Follow same pattern as `ShareDialog.tsx:368-370` (zeroing itemFolderKey).

   292→### Pitfall 5: OpenAPI Client Not Regenerated
   293→
   294→**What goes wrong:** New invite endpoints exist on the server but the web app has no typed client functions to call them.
   295→**Why it happens:** Must run `pnpm api:generate` after adding/modifying controllers, but it's easy to forget.
   296→**How to avoid:** Run `pnpm api:generate` after implementing any new controller endpoints. Commit the generated files in `apps/web/src/api/`.

   299→### Pitfall 6: Invite Lookup Must Not Require Authentication
   300→
   301→**What goes wrong:** The GET endpoint to fetch invite metadata (for the landing page) requires JWT auth, but the user hasn't authenticated yet.
   302→**Why it happens:** The `SharesController` uses `@UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard)` at the class level (line 41).

   306→2. Use `@Public()` decorator on the GET endpoint (if NestJS module supports it)
   307→3. Create a minimal unauthenticated controller dedicated to invite lookup

   310→
   311→**What goes wrong:** Two recipients click the same link simultaneously, both claim successfully.
   312→**Why it happens:** Read-check-write pattern without locking.
   313→**How to avoid:** Use database-level atomic update: `UPDATE share_invites SET status = 'claimed', claimed_by = :userId, claim_count = claim_count + 1 WHERE token = :token AND status = 'active' AND claim_count < max_claims`. Check `affected === 1`.

   555→
   556→### Server-Side Claim Logic
   557→
   558→The claim endpoint should:
   559→
   560→1. **Validate invite** -- token exists, status is 'active', not expired
   561→2. **Atomic status update** -- `UPDATE ... SET status='claimed', claimed_by=:userId WHERE status='active'` to prevent race conditions
   562→3. **Create Share record** -- reuse parts of `SharesService.createShare()` but with different inputs (no recipientPublicKey lookup needed since we have userId)
   563→4. **Create ShareKey records** -- from the re-wrapped child keys sent by the client
   564→5. **Return shareId** -- client navigates to shared content

   571→2. Fetch invite to verify it's still active (lightweight check)
   572→3. Get recipient's vault keypair from auth store
   573→4. Unwrap `invite.encryptedKey` with ephemeral private key
   574→5. Re-wrap with recipient's public key
   575→6. Do the same for all `encryptedChildKeys`
   576→7. POST claim with re-wrapped keys

The only "leakage" is that someone with the server token can see there IS an invite, which is already implied by the token existing.

| importTssKey via localStorage one-time read-and-delete                 | 12-05     | PnP migration key consumed once then removed                                                                         |
| E2E uses CipherBox login UI directly (no modal iframe)                 | 12-05     | Simpler, more reliable than Web3Auth modal automation                                                                |
| jose library for identity JWTs (not @nestjs/jwt)                       | 12-01     | Separate signing keys (RS256) and audience from internal                                                             |

| Wallet addr: SHA-256 hash + truncated display (no encrypt)             | 12.3-01   | Simpler than hash+encrypted; full plaintext never stored                                                             |
| Auth types: email_passwordless->email, external_wallet->wallet         | 12.3-01   | Clean method-based naming for simplified auth type system                                                            |
